key_insight: Direct stochastic optimization of PV-battery dispatch cuts expected carbon emissions far more effectively than rule-based control, approaching the omniscient lower bound.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that tractable linear programming can guide low-carbon battery operation in residential PV-BESS systems under uncertainty.
method: Compared a hierarchy of linear battery control models from heuristic self-consumption to stochastic optimization with linear feedback.
Modeled uncertain household load, solar output, and grid carbon intensity using large scenario sets generated from real data via PCA.
Evaluated emission-minimizing dispatch on synthetic yet realistic operating scenarios.
evidence_signal: Computational experiments on synthetic realistic scenarios showed the programmed battery model substantially outperformed heuristic control and nearly matched the omniscient benchmark.
watch_item: Feedback-based models improved training performance only marginally and did not generalize better on unseen data, while increasing computational cost.
paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Linear Battery Models for Carbon Emission Optimization in Solar Energy Systems
